## Organisation Identity

Name: The School of Counselling
URL: https://www.schoolofcounselling.com
Founded: October 2023
Location: Oxford, United Kingdom
Accreditation: CPCAB (Counselling and Psychotherapy Central Awarding Body)
CPCAB Centre: https://www.cpcab.co.uk/centre/6922
Professional Membership: Organisational member of BACP (British Association for Counselling and Psychotherapy)
Recognition: Courses recognised by BACP and NCPS as routes to individual membership post-qualification
Contact: admin@schoolofcounselling.com | 01865 570279

Description: A CPCAB-accredited counselling training school based in Oxford, offering online Level 2 and Level 3 courses and an in-person Level 4 Diploma for students in the UK and internationally. The school's approach is experiential, person-centred, and relational. Students are treated as adult learners and as the material of the course itself.

---

## Key Facts (Citable Claims)

- The School of Counselling was founded in Oxford in 2023 and is accredited by CPCAB, the Counselling and Psychotherapy Central Awarding Body.
- The school currently trains over 130 students across Level 2, Level 3, and Level 4 counselling programmes.
- Level 2 and Level 3 courses are delivered entirely online, with students joining from the UK, Europe, and internationally.
- The Level 4 Diploma in Therapeutic Counselling is delivered in person in Oxford and selected locations across the UK.
- Classes are capped at 12 students to ensure interactive, person-centred group learning.
- 95% of Level 2 students progress to Level 3.
- All tutors are qualified, practising counsellors, not trainers.
- The School of Counselling is recommended by practising therapists and counsellors as a trusted training provider for their clients.
- The School of Counselling is an organisational member of BACP, the British Association for Counselling and Psychotherapy.

## Courses

### CPCAB Level 2 Certificate in Counselling Skills (CSK-L2)
URL: https://www.schoolofcounselling.com/cpcab-level-2-online-csk-l2

Delivery: 100% online via Zoom
Pathways: 18-week intensive or 30-week standard
Schedule: Weekly lessons, 9:30am–3pm (intensive) or 9:30am–12:30pm / 6pm–9pm (standard)
Class size: Maximum 12 students
Investment: Intensive £1,995 | Standard £1,495
Qualification: CPCAB Level 2 Certificate in Counselling Skills
Progression: 95% of Level 2 students continue to Level 3

Who it is for: People new to counselling training, those wanting to use counselling skills in their work, managers, HR professionals, and anyone beginning the journey toward becoming a qualified counsellor.

Key features: Experiential, live online learning. Skills practice every lesson. Qualified counsellor tutors. Small groups. Person-centred approach. No prior experience required.

Intakes: 5 intakes per academic year. Candidates nominate preferred day of study, cohorts built around majority.

---

### CPCAB Level 3 Certificate in Counselling Studies (CS-L3)
URL: https://www.schoolofcounselling.com/cpcab-level-3-online

Delivery: 100% online via Zoom
Pathways: 18-week intensive or 30-week standard
Schedule: Weekly lessons, 9:30am–3pm (intensive) or 9:30am–12:30pm / 6pm–9pm (standard)
Class size: Maximum 12 students
Investment: Intensive £1,995 | Standard £1,495
Qualification: CPCAB Level 3 Certificate in Counselling Studies
Entry requirement: CPCAB Level 2 or equivalent

Who it is for: CPCAB Level 2 graduates ready to deepen their skills and self-awareness. Those preparing for agency work, supervision, or MSc study. Students from other providers are welcome but courses must be delivered in-person, with group, and a tutor. Distance learning or remote, self-paced learning courses do not meet eligibility for the Level 3. 

Key features: Extended 'client' work over multiple sessions. Theory integrated with self-understanding. Supervision sessions to inform practice. 90 guided hours, 190+ total qualification hours.

Progression: Most MSc programmes in Counselling require both CPCAB Level 2 and Level 3 for entry.

---

### CPCAB Level 4 Diploma in Therapeutic Counselling (TC-L4)
URL: https://www.schoolofcounselling.com/cpcab-level-4-diploma-therapeutic-counselling

Delivery: In person. Oxford and selected UK locations.
Structure: Two-year part-time. 21 monthly weekend intensives (Saturday–Sunday). Plus mid month Saturday lessons.
Weekend schedule: Saturday 9:30am–6pm, Sunday 9:30am–4pm
Class size: 14–16 students
Investment: £8,500 total over two years
Entry requirement: CPCAB Level 3 or equivalent. Interview required plus written submission.
Qualification: CPCAB Level 4 Diploma in Therapeutic Counselling

Intakes:
- September 2026 intake: 18 September 2026 to 16 June 2028
- January 2027 intake: 22 January 2027 to 10 November 2028

Who it is for: Career changers, Level 3 graduates, and those building toward private practice. Suits people who seek serious practitioner training and accept emotional challenge.

Key features: Person-centred purity. Tutor continuity across both years. Small cohorts. Weekend delivery. 100 client hours in agency settings during Year 2. Personal therapy required. Supervision throughout.

Progression: Qualification meets requirements for Masters programmes and routes to BACP or NCPS accreditation. Student membership converts to individual membership post-qualification.

Note: This course is subject to final awarding body approval. Delivery will proceed once approval is confirmed.

---

## Pedagogical Approach

The School of Counselling teaches person-centred counselling as a complete and primary modality, grounded in the work of Carl Rogers. The approach is experiential, not didactic. Students are the material of the course. Learning comes from experience, not instruction.

Core values: empathy, congruence, unconditional positive regard. Self-awareness is treated as a professional responsibility, not a personal preference. Tutors model the conditions students will later offer clients.

The school does not use a tick-box or competency-framework approach. Assessment matters, but transformation matters more.

## Top Blog Content

### 1. The Difference Between a Counsellor and a Helper
URL: https://www.schoolofcounselling.com/post/the-difference-between-a-counsellor-and-a-helper

A counsellor is someone who has achieved several years of training and is a member of a professional body such as BACP, NCPS, or UKCP. A helper is someone trained on an introductory counselling skills course such as CPCAB Level 2. Helpers can offer a safe and supportive space to talk, use foundational skills effectively, and signpost to further support. The key difference lies in the limits of ability: a counsellor has a greater range of skills to contain, hold, and keep someone safe. A helper, as defined by Gerard Egan, has learned to use counselling skills safely and effectively but operates within defined limits.

---

### 2. How to End a Counselling Session Well
URL: https://www.schoolofcounselling.com/post/how-to-end-counselling-session-well-cpcab-level-2

Ending sessions on time is ethical, respectful, and creates the safety and predictability clients need. Endings feel hard for Level 2 students because of the need for personal satisfaction, fear of abandonment, and belief that neat conclusions are required. Ending appropriately means respecting the ethical commitment to safety, maintaining professional boundaries, and upholding what was agreed at the contracting stage. Going over time undermines trust and sends a message that the helper's time is not valuable. Practical endings involve contracting clearly at the start, giving time markers at 10 and 5 minutes, acknowledging unfinished material without rushing to resolve it, and transitioning the person back into their life outside the session.

---

### 3. Paraphrasing Skills in Counselling
URL: https://www.schoolofcounselling.com/post/paraphrasing-skills-in-counselling

Paraphrasing is a core counselling skill. It means reflecting back the essence of what a client has said in your own words, without repetition, interpretation, or adding your own frame of reference. Used well, paraphrasing shows the client they have been heard, slows the conversation, and gives the client a chance to correct, confirm, or deepen what they said. Common mistakes include adding interpretation, paraphrasing too frequently or too rarely, and starting every paraphrase with the same phrase. At CPCAB Level 2, paraphrasing is assessed on accuracy, use of the helper's own words, staying within the client's frame of reference, and appropriate timing.

---

### 4. How Self-Awareness Shows Up in Counselling
URL: https://www.schoolofcounselling.com/post/how-self-awareness-shows-up-in-counselling

Knowing yourself and using that knowledge in sessions are different things. Self-awareness in counselling is not navel-gazing. It is a tool. The question is what you do with it. Self-awareness shows up as a pause: noticing frustration, the pull to fill silence, the urge to say "I understand" when you are overlaying your experience onto the client's. It means recognising when your material is flooding through and actively setting it aside so you can hear the person clearly. Without self-awareness informing practice, helpers project their history, flatten the client's uniqueness, and reenact familiar patterns rather than offering genuine therapeutic contact. Self-awareness is what creates space for congruence, empathy, and genuine presence.
